pipelineDefectsFixed.where: ffone-asset-pipeline logical_model_publish, ffone-skinned-model validate, ffone-client legacy_model_material
pipelineDefectsFixed.defect: all three treated `unassignedSlot` as necessarily nameless with a null pointer, but the exporter also marks a *named* slot unassigned when its PPtr names no object. Twelve modded NPCs carry `_ShaderMap` with uninitialised bytes in the pointer (file ids near 163774465 while the sibling `_MainTex` of the same material uses file id 0) and were refused.
pipelineDefectsFixed.fix: both unassigned shapes are accepted; neither may carry a texture payload, and only the nameless shape may carry a null pointer

pipelineDefectsFixed.defect: the installer demanded a `<name>.textures` directory even for a model that publishes no texture at all
pipelineDefectsFixed.fix: a missing closure is accepted when the GLB has no assigned texture binding; npc_paradox and npc_azmuth bind an explicitly null `_MainTex` because the runtime dresses them from the NPC table's Texture1/Texture2

server.conclusion: the server XDT needs no change: every field the OpenFusion source reads from m_pNpcData is identical for all 43 rows. Only m_iMesh and m_iIcon1 differ, and no source file in OpenFusion/src reads either -- the complete set of m_i*/m_f* field names the server reads was enumerated to confirm it.

spawnData.finding: none of the 43 ids is spawned. This is faithful to the modded build rather than a gap: all 43 of the modding tool's own npc-import records carry spawnMap, spawnPosition, spawnAngle and spawnJsonId as null, so the modded client never placed them either. Placing them is level design and is not invented here.
